title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
summary: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini, and Jeff Mason as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump’s Foes Find Common Ground at Modi’s New Delhi Summit
summary: Leaders of emerging powers including Russia and Iran projected a united front at a weekend summit in New Delhi, with a joint statement that targeted a US-launched war in the Middle East, Washington’s tariff campaign and its sanctions policy.

title: Iran War Revives Lessons of Iraq for Fukuyama
summary: Joining David Gura on Bloomberg This Weekend, Stanford Spogli Institute for International Studies Senior Fellow Francis Fukuyama says the Iran war risks repeating lessons from Iraq and Afghanistan, arguing that military power alone is unlikely to produce lasting political change. In discussing his new memoir, In the Realm of the Last Man, he also warns that the rapid advance of AI could outpace governments' ability to regulate it and challenge the role that work plays in giving people purpose. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Energy Driven Inflation Complicates Fed Rate Call
summary: PNC Chief Investment Officer Amanda Agati is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says the Fed faces a difficult decision as energy-driven inflation pushes markets toward expectations for higher rates, warning that further tightening could risk a policy error. Agati also tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini investors are also adjusting to the prospect of a longer Iran war, while strong corporate earnings have pushed concerns about AI spending further into the background. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Number of Vessels Redirected in US Blockade on Iran Reaches 100
summary: US forces have redirected 100 commercial vessels over the past 60 days since the blockade against Iran resumed, the Central Command says in an update on X.

title: Xi Resets Ties With Modi on First Visit to India in Seven Years
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi moved closer to overcoming years of frictions over issues including an unresolved border dispute, holding a meeting in New Delhi that signaled a reset of ties between the world’s two most populous countries.

title: Iran Nuclear Blind Spot Deepens as IAEA Loses Access
summary: Former US Energy Secretary Ernest Moniz says the loss of IAEA access to Iran has created a serious monitoring gap that makes it increasingly difficult to determine the status of the country's nuclear program. Moniz also warns hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that tight global supplies of diesel and other refined fuels could face additional pressure as US refineries, already running near capacity, approach their fall maintenance season. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Luxury Shoppers Put Value Ahead of Labels
summary: Bloomberg Pursuits Global Luxury Editor editor Chris Rovzar says luxury shoppers are increasingly prioritizing price, quality and lasting value over labels, helping brands such as Coach and Ralph Lauren gain ground as parts of the broader luxury industry struggle. Joining David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend, Rovzar explains that New York Fashion Week is also showing renewed momentum for American fashion, with heritage brands and designers embracing color, archival influences and more accessible luxury. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: RBI Said to Reject Tata Sons Request to Avoid An IPO
summary: India’s central bank rejected an application from Tata Sons Pvt. to surrender its status as a shadow lender, according to people familiar with the matter, signaling it expects the company to adhere with rules for such entities that include an initial public offering.

title: AI Agents Test the Limits of Human Control
summary: Future of Life Institute Chair & Co-Founder Max Tegmark joins Bloomberg This Weekend and says recent incidents involving autonomous AI agents show that loss-of-control risks are no longer purely theoretical and warrant stronger safety requirements. OpenAI has acknowledged that its agents circumvented controls, communicated through unauthorized channels and breached Hugging Face during testing, incidents that are fueling renewed debate over federal AI oversight. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Higher Interest Rates May Be the New Normal
summary: Joining Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics Chief Economist Tom Orlik says higher interest rates may be the new normal, leaving governments, businesses and households facing a mounting cost from debt accumulated during years of cheap borrowing. Orlik tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh faces a key test at next week's meeting as markets signal expectations for tighter policy, potentially putting the central bank at odds with President Donald Trump's preference for lower rates.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Europe’s Solar Boom Has a Storage Problem
summary: Solar has become Europe’s largest source of power during summer months, helped by government incentives, falling technology costs and a rapid buildout across rooftops and utility-scale projects. But that success is creating a new problem: on sunny days, Europe can produce more solar power than the system can absorb, pushing wholesale electricity prices to zero or below and leaving some renewable generators suffering from their own success. Industry experts say the answer is not less solar, but more storage, more flexible demand and stronger grids that can move power from where it is generated to where it is needed. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ‘Crazy’ French Inversion Shows Credit Is a Haven: Credit Weekly
summary: Bond traders are making an unusual judgment about risk in French financial markets: they believe collateralized bank bonds are safer than government debt.

title: Iran Nuclear Activity Raises New Concerns
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Council on Foreign Relations senior fellow Ray Takeyh says renewed Houthi attacks represent a significant setback for the US strategy of stabilizing regional oil flows and may indicate closer coordination between the group and Iran. Takeyh also tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that economic pressure has failed to force Tehran to change course, as new construction at the deeply buried Pickaxe Mountain complex raises questions about the future of Iran's nuclear program. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
summary: College athletes buy million-dollar homes, 'sudden wealth syndrome,' Princess Diana's 'revenge dress' on auction, snoring sleep partners could impact your health: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini as they go over interesting headlines from this week. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Supply Risks Rise After Saudi Pipeline Attack
summary: Saudi Arabia shut its East-West Pipeline as a precaution after multiple attacks, threatening a crucial route for moving crude to the Red Sea while bypassing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg Economics' Ziad Daoud says prolonged disruption could tighten global energy supplies further, adding pressure to oil and US diesel prices. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Modi Seeks BRICS Unity as Global Tensions Rise
summary: India is seeking to forge consensus among an expanded BRICS membership despite divergent positions on the Iran war, relations with the US and the bloc's role in the global order. Joining David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend is Bloomberg News Senior Reporter Dan Strumpf who explains that the summit is also highlighting a tentative India-China rapprochement, with President Xi Jinping visiting New Delhi and China Southern Airlines preparing to restore its Guangzhou-New Delhi service after a six-year suspension. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: BRICS 2026: Modi Seeks Bigger Role For Global South
summary: India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeks bigger role for BRICS nations in setting global rules. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Signals US Wants Distance From Iran War
summary: President Donald Trump is playing down prospects for renewed Iran peace talks and broader US involvement even as Houthi activity adds another source of escalation to the conflict. Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason joins Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss President Trump's statements made during the Presidents trip to Ireland. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Iraq Fires Maysan Commander After Drone Attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Pipeline
summary: The closure of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline sparked further fallout on Saturday after the attacks were determined to have been launched from inside Iraq.
